match.reason: None of the bank points explains that Australian rainfall is driven by El Niño and La Niña, which is the central idea of the new point; the closest card, Why water supply varies, only notes that some years are wetter or drier without giving the cause.

draft.title: Variable rainfall in Australia
card: Variable rainfall means the amount of rain changes a lot from year to year. Australia has wet years and dry years, and a place can swing from one to the other.
a pattern in the Pacific Ocean that is often linked to drier years in eastern and northern Australia. It does not always bring drought.
a pattern in the Pacific Ocean that is often linked to wetter years in eastern and northern Australia. It does not always bring floods.
Because rainfall swings so much, droughts and floods are both common. Dams store water in wet years so that people can use it in dry years.
draft.remember: Rainfall swings from year to year. El Niño is often drier, La Niña is often wetter, and dams store water for dry years.

a.q: What does it mean to say Australia's rainfall is variable?
opts: The amount of rain changes a lot from year to year
Rain falls evenly across the country each year
Rain falls only in the wet season each year
The amount of rain slowly rises every year
a.why: Variable means rainfall changes a lot from one year to the next, with wet years and dry years. Rain falling evenly would mean the amount stays steady, which is the opposite of variable.
a.clue: Think about how rain differs from one year to the next.

b.q: A wheat farmer near Dubbo has had several dry years, and the Pacific Ocean is in an El Niño pattern. Why might the town's dam have been built?
opts: To store water in wet years for use in dry years
To stop La Niña from bringing rain to the town
To make rainfall the same in every year
To store water because El Niño always brings drought
b.why: Rainfall swings between wet and dry years, so dams hold water from wet years to use when it is dry. The last option is tempting, but El Niño is often linked to drier years, not always, and dams are built because of the swings in rainfall.
b.clue: Dams help when rainfall is uneven from year to year.

a.best: The amount of rain changes a lot from year to year

b.best: To store water in wet years for use in dry years

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the 'always brings drought' option 'the last option', but options are shown in random order, and in this list the last option is the La Niña one. The explanation should name the option by its content, not its position.

Why (a) says rain falling evenly 'would mean the amount stays steady', but the option 'Rain falls evenly across the country each year' is about rain spread across places (point 4), not change over time. The explanation mixes up the two ideas and could confuse students.
